title: slo-alarm-chaining-circuit-breaker-prototype-notes
content:
Summary:

Prototype notes for an alarm-chaining + circuit-breaker approach to reduce pager noise from SLO burn storms and transient missing metrics. Goal: keep real reliability signal while suppressing follow-on alarms that are consequences of an upstream failure or noisy metric feed.

Context / motivation:
- Over the last 6 months we've seen 3 production incidents where a single upstream degraded dependency (auth cache, model routing) produced a cascade of SLO alerts across 4 services. On-call pages ballooned and responders chased noisy symptoms (downstream timeouts) rather than root cause.
- Separate class of incidents: intermittent exporter flaps / metrics pipeline delays causing SLOs to spike because of missing buckets or delayed histograms. These generate immediate paging for teams that have low-noise thresholds.
- Current gap: alert groups/quiet windows reduce volume but are static and brittle. We need a runtime mechanism that understands relationships between signals and can temporarily circuit-break (suppress) downstream alarms when the upstream problem is primary or when metric presence is uncertain.

Observed incidents (examples):
1) 2026-01-18 - model-routing flake -> frontend 99th latency SLO burn -> embedding-service error spike -> 4 teams paged. Root cause: routing table refresh failure in dedicated pool. Time to mitigate: 47m. Pager-hours: ~6.
2) 2026-02-09 - metrics-exporter OOM -> missing latency buckets for apiproxy -> SLO for apiproxy jumped -> oncall paged even though backend traces showed healthy requests. Root cause: exporter memory leak. Time to mitigate: 1h 10m.

Principles for design:
- Chain alarms rather than duplicate them: annotate primary signal, mark dependent alerts as "consequent" and suppress paging while surfacing to dashboards.
- Fail-open for missing observability: if metric ingestion is uncertain, generate a low-severity notice rather than a full page immediately; escalate if missingness persists beyond a grace window (configurable by SLO).
- Keep humans in the loop: provide a single, actionable root-cause page with suggested investigation steps and a link to correlated traces/logs.
- Config driven, with safe defaults: teams can opt out or tune thresholds.

Prototype design (high-level):
- Components:
  - Signal Router (SR): service that receives normalized alert signals (SLO burn, error-rate, missing-metrics sentinel) and owns short-lived alarm state for correlations.
  - Chaining rules engine: simple DAG where nodes are alert types and edges have confidence weights + suppression TTLs.
  - Circuit-breaker service: when SR marks a node as upstream primary and confidence > threshold, it suppresses downstream paging for X minutes, posts a consolidated incident to the incident system, and notifies owners via non-pager channel (Slack incident thread + dashboard link).
  - Missing-metrics detector: consumes exporter heartbeat and histogram coverage; produces a "metric-absence" signal with severity proportional to coverage loss and duration.

- Example rule (pseudo):
  IF slo:frontend_p99_burn AND slo:embeddings_error_rate rises within 2m AND correlation(confidence) >= 0.7 THEN mark frontend_p99 as primary; suppress embeddings paging for 20m; create consolidated incident 'routing:frontend_p99-cascade-<ts>'

Missing metrics handling:
- Use exporter heartbeats + histogram-bucket coverage to compute a 0..1 metric-coverage score per service.
- If coverage < 0.6 => emit metric-absence signal severity=warning (no page), start 15m timer. If persists after 15m, escalate to page to owner oncall.
- For SLOs computed from percentiles: if dependent histogram missing buckets, switch SLO to 'degraded calculation' mode and post explanatory note to dashboards.

Operational controls and safety:
- Default suppression TTLs small (5-20m) and exponential backoff for repeated suppressions.
- All suppressions are auditable in the incident timeline with the chain reasoning and inputs that triggered suppression.
- Immediate manual override via incident console ("force page downstream").

Metrics to validate prototype (what we measure in the canary rollout):
- Pager count per incident (target: -40% for chained incidents)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for primary incidents (should not increase)
- False suppression rate (cases where downstream suppression hid an independent failure)
- Time-to-detect for missing metrics (should improve because of dedicated signal)
- Pager-hours saved vs oncall impact (qualitative feedback)

Small-scale experiment plan:
1) Lab / replay: feed SR with historical alerts from Jan-Feb incidents and verify chaining decisions. Re-run with knob variations (confidence threshold 0.6/0.7/0.85) to build ROC. Linked: Linear ENGSRE-3421.
2) Canary: enable chaining for 2 non-critical downstream services (staging) and route alerts through SR with suppression but no paging (notifications only). Run for 72h.
3) Soft-prod: enable paging suppression for a single team in prod with strict TTLs and manual overrides. Monitor metrics above + weekly oncall survey.
4) Full prod: roll to more teams after 2-week stability.

Runbook snippets (starter troubleshooting for consolidated incident):
- Step 1: Check SR incident summary -> which upstream node is primary? (field: primary_node)
- Step 2: Jump to suggested traces: click first matching trace at the top of the SR panel (populates filtered trace query)
- Step 3: Validate if metrics ingestion is healthy: check exporter heartbeat panel, histogram coverage score
- Step 4: If primary upstream is distinct (e.g. model-router), follow dedicated router runbook (link below)
- Step 5: If suppression was applied incorrectly, click "force downstream page" and annotate why (audit trail stored)

Runbook TODOs (practical items):
- [ ] Add runbook link for model-router quick fixes (owner: Jonah) - GitHub PR #1422 referenced.
- [ ] Document how teams can opt-out per-SLO (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Create dashboard tiles for metric-coverage by service (owner: Sophie)
- [ ] Write playbook for false-suppression incidents and rollback procedures (owner: Ravi)

Edge cases and open questions:
- How to handle multi-primary incidents where two upstreams fail concurrently? Proposal: compare confidence * impact and avoid double-suppression; escalate to hybrid incident that pages all owners.
- Can attackers intentionally create silencers by flapping metrics? Need rate limits and abuse detection on the SR inputs.
- Is the latency of SR acceptable for low-latency SLO paging (we must ensure <500ms decision time for 99th percentile detection)? Performance targets to be added.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight: the intent is to reduce noisy follow-on pages and improve focus for oncall. Looking for feedback on suppression TTL defaults and the suggested confidence metric formula (simple weighted co-occurrence + causal hints from service graph).
- Please add any examples of recent incidents that would have benefited from chaining (tag them in Linear ENGSRE-3421).

Quick links & references:
- Incident replay dataset: gs://redwood-observability/replays/2026-q1/ (restricted)
- Correlated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1422
- Linear ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENGSRE-3421/alert-chaining-prototype

Session notes (raw, unpolished):
- 2026-03-02 10:15 sync: Maya pushed idea to use histogram coverage as a gate. Sophie: dashboard is doable in 2 days. Jonah: main risk is false suppression during independent downstream failures. Ravi: start conservative TTLs.
- Questions to product: do we expose a "suppress downstream" toggle in service-level config or SLO-level? (product input needed)
- Slack threads: #sre-observability (see pinned messages March threads)

Sign-off plan:
- Aim to merge prototype SR + basic rules engine to staging by 2026-03-18. After successful replay tests, schedule canary and stakeholder review.
